2 Rules & Strategies

Author: Date: To start developing the strategies for the competition, we have to first look at how the game is played. Override Rules 2026/5/7 CY 31 The scoring objects for Override are pins and cups. Pins come in different colors and cups have two sides. The placement and arrangement of these objects are key. The override field is split into four quadrants and one midfield in the center. Scores from the yellow pins in each zone are determined at the end of the game. We will explore the rules further in the upcoming pages.

Author: Date: The core of Override is the strategic placement of pins and cups. Rules - Scoring 2026/5/7 CY 32 For each half of the pins colored in red or blue scored, the corresponding alliance gets 5 points. The yellow pins can be worth 10 points. This is done if the yellow half of a pin is scored on a goal located a zone that an alliance controls. For quadrants, an alliance can control it by flipping the toggle to their color. The yellow pins on the middle goal go to the team with most robots in the midfield at the end of the match. Also, for each robot in the midfield at the end of the match, their alliance earns 8 points. Also, possession is always limited to one cup and one pin. So, cycle time is going to be key. Cups come in one transparent side and one black side. The black side of the cup basically blocks one side of the pin. Essentially, you can “override” existing pins.

Author: Date: Expansion rules are also really important since they will change how we design our robot. Rules - Expansion & Endgame 2026/5/7 CY 33 During the match, the horizontal expansion is limited to a 24” x 24” square. However, vertical expansion can go up to 50 inches tall, around the height of 7 pins stacked on a neutral goal. First, the robot starting configuration has to be within an 18” x 18” x 18” cube, which is the same size as the previous season, Push Back. In the last 20 seconds of the match, vertical expansion shrinks to 18” if a robot is partially in the midfield. Ending the match with the robot partially in the midfield yields 8 points. And the alliance with more robots in the midfield get points of the yellow pins on the center goal. So the rush to midfield in the end is really important. *Image source in Appendix

Author: Date: Goals are where pins and cups are placed to score points. There are 9 goals in total - 2 alliance goals for each alliance, 4 short neutral goals, and 1 tall neutral goal in the center. Rules - Goals 2026/5/7 CY 34 According to <SG9>, teams can’t touch, score, and descore on the opposite colored alliance goals. Another huge rule in Override is <SG10>, which bans the action of removing objects from all goals except the team’s own alliance goals. The GDC encourages using the dark side of the cups to override pins instead of descoring by removing objects. Since descoring is not allowed, we should score in the neutral goals early on so the opponents have less scoring opportunities on the neutral goals. Also, we have to be careful not to touch opponents’ alliance goals.

Author: Date: Autonomous period is 15 seconds long. The main goal of auto is to earn the Autonomous Bonus of 12 points and the Autonomous Win Point. Rules - Autonomous 2026/5/7 CY 35 The AWP should be our primary consideration when designing our robot and the autonomous route. The main challenge is to score 7 pins. To win the autonomous bonus, we have to score more points than the opponents during the autonomous period. To achieve this goal, activating the toggles and stacking yellow pins are the optimal actions. Also, the autonomous line is drawn in a way that the midfield is open to both alliances. So it is a more dangerous place to go during auto.

Author: Date: Let’s make conclusions. First, looking back to the different methods of scoring, we see that the autonomous bonus gives 12 points, which is super high. Each robot in the midfield gives 8 points, which is also high considering it is super easy to touch the midfield. Now, although yellow pins score twice as much as alliance pins, they are super risky as they could easily flip to the opponents by simply turning the toggles. Conclusion & Strategy 2026/5/7 CY 36 To recap, here are our strategies for Override: Autonomous: Toggle + Yellows to score high and get the autonomous bonus while completing missions for the AWP. Driving Period: Use match loads to build up towers of our color. Prioritize the neutral goals to block opponents. Endgame: Rush to midfield for an extra 8 points. Also, tell our teammates to do the same.

Author: Date: Control algorithms are core to all automation in our robot program. Using different control algorithms and combining them can allow our motors make more accurate and smooth movement. The following are common algorithms in VEX Robotics and we plan to explore and implement this in our robot control programs: 1. PID Controller : A reactive control algorithm. PID stands for proportional, integral, and derivative. It helps motors quickly and smoothly move to the target. 2. Feed Forward Control : A proactive control algorithm. It predicts the required power with known factors. Reduces delay by anticipating disturbances. 3. Motion Profiling : An algorithm that calculates a smooth schedule of positions and velocity. This prevents violent acceleration and jerk by structuring phases of acceleration, cruising, and deceleration. Control Algorithms 2026/6/4 CY 103

Author: Date: Before we start programming, we have to understand how the PID controller works first. PID Controller Overview 2026/6/4 CY 104 “Matthias random stuff” uploaded a great video explaining how the PID controller works. The video shows the purposes of each part of the PID controller and demonstrates the consequences of setting constants too large or too little. P, I, and D controllers explained in simple terms: Proportional: Turns the motor power up when current position is far away from the target (big error). Integral: Prevents the “steady state error” by accumulating tiny errors. Derivative: Prevents overshooting by applying brakes based on the rate of change of the error. *Image source in Appendix

Author: Date: The core of PID controller lies in the P(proportional) part. The proportional controller acts like a spring: the farther our robot is from the target, the stronger the force it generates. The constant Kp acts like the spring constant of a spring. It determines how sensitive the controller is. Proportional Controller 2026/6/4 CY 105 A Kp too high causes overshooting problems and end up making oscillations because the controller is too sensitive. On the other hand, a Kp too low makes the controller have a hard time reaching the target Balancing the Kp is very important for a PID controller. However, even with an optimal Kp value, there are still problems and limitations.

Author: Date: A problem of the proportional controller is the steady state error. When the error distance is too small, so is the motor output. This small motor output is sometimes not enough to overcome friction. If the robot stays in a steady state, then the integral controller would accumulate the tiny error and push the robot towards the target. The constant Ki determines the influence of the accumulated error. Integral Controller 2026/6/4 CY 106 With only the proportional controller, the current position would not reach the target due to the steady state error. Adding the Ki helps eliminate the steady state error. However, a Ki too large causes the curve to oscillate more.

Author: Date: The purpose of the derivative controller is to prevent overshooting and oscillation. With only the proportional and integral controllers, it takes a long time to reach a stable state. The derivative controller looks at the rate of change of the error distance. If the robot is approaching the error too quickly, the derivative slows down the motors a little bit to prevent overshooting. The constant Kd determines how much the controller reacts to the rate of change of the error. Derivative Controller 2026/6/4 CY 107 Without the derivative controller, the robot would easily overshoot, especially the first spike. Adding the derivative controller can reduce or even eliminate the overshooting problems. However, a Kd too large creates violent oscillation.

Author: Date: When playing with the integral controller, we noticed that a high Ki makes the oscillations really big. This is due to huge errors being accumulated, impacting the motor output by a lot. So, these two optimizations are applied. Integral Optimization 2026/6/4 CY 108 The first optimization is setting “maxi.” We should only integrate the errors smaller than maxi. This prevents huge error from ruining the I controller. The other optimization is resetting the accumulated error when the error crosses 0. This prevents the error accumulated long ago from impacting. Without the optimizations, the integral controller is really dangerous and unstable. By only accumulating small errors and resetting the accumulated error when the error crosses zero allows the integral controller to be safe and effective.

Author: Date: Feedforward is all about considering known, predictable forces and countering them before they even happen. Feedforward 2026/6/5 CY 115 Feedforward is a proactive control algorithm that influences the system without reading the output. PID, on the other hand is a reactive algorithm that depends on the output. Normally, a feedforward controller is comprised of 3 parts, corresponding to the stall, velocity, and acceleration controllers. First, a certain power is needed to kickstart the system, this is known as Ks . Then, to sustain the system at a fixed speed, power is also needed. The constant Kv multiplied by the velocity is its output. Finally, power is also needed to accelerate the system. The constant Ka multiplied by the acceleration is its power. *Image source in Appendix

Author: Date: Although we could use the constant Ks to maintain the lift at a certain height, it is a better practice to make the lift able to stay at a height with rubber bands. Basically, the rubber bands act like a mechanical feedforward. Lift Rubber Bands 2026/6/5 CY 116 First, we tried triangle banding by adding 3 screws on the 4 bar lift and band them together. However, it made the lift super hard to lift up. After looking online for dr4b builds, we saw that they only connect the bands with 2 points. We did the same thing as well, except that the third points extends the rubber bands. After messing with the positions of the screws, we finally managed to make the lift almost sustain its height at all levels. This reduces the motor’s strain when lifting up. Also, we don’t need the constant Ks in our feedforward program now.

Author: Date: In order to make our movement curve smooth and mathematically constrained. We decided to use an algorithm called motion profiling. Basically, the motion profile generator calculates the target position and target velocity at each time cycle based on the maximum acceleration and velocity allowed. Motion Profiling 2026/6/5 CY 117 Motion profiling basically makes the velocity versus time graph show a trapezoid. When looking at the position versus time graph, a smooth s-curve can be seen. The acceleration and deceleration phases stabilize the curve. In our code, the target position generated by the profile will be fed into the PID controller while the target velocity will be fed into the feedforward controller.

Author: Date: The way we could accomplish motion profiling is also through a class object. A trapezoidal profile object contains the variables limiting the maximum acceleration and velocity allowed. Its update function gives the new target position and velocity. Motion Profile Class 2026/6/5 CY 118 First, we define a struct object called “ProfileState” which contains the target position and velocity. This struct is the input and output of the profile function. The class structure of the profile is rather simple. It has 2 variables, the object constructor, and the update function that calculates the next profile state based on the current profile and the ultimate target.

Author: Date: The update function of the trapezoidal profile isn’t complicated too. Motion Profile Code 2026/6/5 CY 119 Basically, target velocity is added with the maximum allowed acceleration until it reaches the maximum velocity allowed. When it hits the calculated braking distance, target velocity is subtracted instead. Finally, the new target position for PID and the new target velocity for feedforward is returned.

Author: Date: Next, we used PID to chase the target position calculated by our motion profile. Motion Profile Test 2026/6/5 CY 120 First, we tried Kp = 1 and Kd = 10. It created a beautiful S curve. However, it takes 0.6s to reach the target, which is a bit too long. Then, we changed the Kp to 5. As a result, we managed to reach the target a lot earlier. However, the initial overshooting is too big. Finally, we changed the Kp down to 2. We can still reach the target under 0.4s while eliminating the overshooting problem.

Author: Date: Next, we decided to test the velocity feedforward. We paired it up with the motion profile. The only source of power of motors is from the velocity feedforward controller. Feedforward Test 2026/6/5 CY 121 First, we went for Kv = 12 to give it maximum power. However, the overshooting problem is huge, and it couldn’t resist against gravity after the profile ends. Next, we went for Kv = 10. We could almost reach the target and the S shape looks nice. Again, the lift couldn’t sustain its height due to gravity. Since feedforward is a pure proactive algorithm, it has no feedback and no way of correcting itself. This is why we still need the reactive PID controller. Combining feedforward and PID should be optimal.

Author: Date: Finally, we combined PID with feedforward along with motion profiling. The goals are to reach the target as soon as possible, not overshoot, and stabilize quickly. PID + Feedforward Test 2026/6/5 CY 122 For the velocity feedforward controller, we chose Kv = 10. Then, we chose Kp = 1 first to see what happens. We can see some overshooting problems. Next, we tried Kp = 0.2. However, we weren’t able to reach the target. And since we don’t have Ki added, the huge steady state error just continues to stay. Finally, we set Kp to 0.5 with a bit Ki and Kd added. Although there is still some tiny error after reaching the target, it is overall really fast and stable.
